segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, thanks for making time, Karen. I wanted to confirm the 42 seats for the support team and the five manager seats before I send the order form for the June 1 start.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That’s right. We’re at 37 active reps today, but the next training class starts June 10, so 42 gives us a little room. Managers stay at five.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Got it. The annual subscription comes to $28,560, and implementation is the one-time $3,200 we discussed. Billing would be net 30, invoice sent after signature, unless you need a PO first.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: We do need a PO. Finance said they can turn it around in two business days if the quote has the tax line and the service dates on it.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yep, I’ve got service dates as June 1, 2026 through May 31, 2027. Tax is estimated at $1,914.72 based on the Chicago office address. If the PO comes back with a different billing entity, we can update that before signature.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay. And just to be clear, we’re doing single sign-on at launch, not later. That was the one thing IT cared about.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Correct. SSO is included in the implementation scope, and the go-live plan has the admin session on May 20 and user training on May 28. If IT wants a separate technical call, I can set that for next week.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Please do. Tuesday after 1 Central works. Also, the contract term, there’s no auto-renewal longer than one year, right?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Right, it renews for successive one-year terms unless either side gives 45 days’ notice. I’ll point that out in the summary email so legal doesn’t have to hunt for it.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Perfect. Send the quote today, and I’ll attach it to the PO request. If procurement doesn’t redline anything weird, we should be able to sign by Friday.
